claims: Most people stop at Gmail + calendar ('chief of staff') but Grok Bot's plugin catalog goes much deeper
AgentMail gives the agent its own email address so it can sign up for tools, receive confirmation codes, and handle correspondence without touching your personal mail
Stripe plugin can move real money, so keep it on restricted permissions until trusted
Combined result: a teammate with its own email, a view of your books, and your publishing calendar
how_to_steps: Install AgentMail plugin to give the agent a dedicated inbox
Install Stripe's official plugin; set restricted permissions first
Install a social posting plugin (Posterly) so the agent that writes content can also schedule it
on_screen_only: AgentMail landing page: 'Give Grok Bot its own inbox - AgentMail is the best way to give Grok Bot its own inbox. Send email, receive replies, and manage full conversation threads from a dedicated inbox.' buttons START FOR FREE / DOCS, 'One command'
Stripe homepage: 'Financial infrastructure to grow your revenue', 'Global GDP running on Stripe'
practicallyai newsletter signup with '37.78x better at AI after 365 days' graphic
cta: Subscribe to the practically.ai daily newsletter

relevance.why: Haji runs Claude, not Grok Bot, but the pattern transfers: give an agent its own inbox (AgentMail has an API/MCP usable from Claude) and connect Stripe with restricted scope. Haji's liked set includes Jarvis-style agents reading Stripe

implement_score.why: AgentMail for the agent's own email is the useful piece (sign-ups, OTP codes, outreach from a separate identity) and takes under an hour via its API/MCP in Claude Code. Stripe read-only MCP is already available for Claude; Posterly is interchangeable with Postiz which Haji already saw
